subject: Burst-mode streaming SLA: waiver request and fallback criteria
messages:
From: Alex Martin <alex.martin@brightbridge.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightbridge.com
Date: Sat, 24 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary SLA carveout for nightly ingestion burst

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Quick background: starting Nov 1 we're onboarding a nightly media ingestion pipeline that spikes to ~2.5M tokens/min for a 20–30 minute window. Normal traffic is orders of magnitude lower. Our compliance team needs explicit SLA language covering time-to-first-token and token/sec expectations for streaming endpoints during these scheduled bursts.

We reviewed the standard Redwood streaming SLO but it focuses on sustained rates and steady-state latency. For our use case we need either:
- a temporary waiver that relaxes token/sec commitments during the defined maintenance window, or
- an agreed fallback behavior (sync endpoint, reduced quality model, or queued ingestion with explicit backpressure) with deterministic RTOs.

Attached is the ingest_profile.csv with traffic shape and a draft schedule. Can Redwood propose a path that minimizes business disruption while preserving contractual clarity?

Thanks,
Alex Martin
Director, Platform Engineering
BrightBridge Health

[Attachment: ingest_profile.csv (csv)]

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Alex Martin <alex.martin@brightbridge.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 24 Oct 2026 12:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA carveout for nightly ingestion burst

Alex — thanks for the data and the clear ask. We can do two parallel things quickly:

1) Technical proposal (ETA: 48 hours) — Karhtik and Aditya will propose a concrete serving/fallback pattern (preferred: prefix caching + short-lived burst pool + deterministic fallback to sync endpoint) with expected TTFT and token/sec ranges for each path.

2) Contractual language (ETA: 3 business days) — Marissa and Stephanie can draft a short addendum that describes the scheduled window, acceptance criteria, and rollback/failure modes. We should also include an audit clause for telemetry during the window.

Quick clarifying Qs to make the proposal tight:
- Are the spikes strictly scheduled (daily 02:00–02:30 PT) or variable?
- What's the acceptable degradation model: reduced per-token throughput, increased latency, or temporary queuing?

I'll kick off the tech readout and loop Legal as needed.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, Alex Martin <alex.martin@brightbridge.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA carveout for nightly ingestion burst

Alex — dug into the ingest_profile.csv and sketched three feasible options (high-level):

Option A — Burst pool + prefix caching (recommended):
- Provision a short-lived dedicated GPU burst pool that scales just for the 20–30 minute window.
- Prefix/KV cache warmup for predictable tails; TTFT target: 150–300 ms for streaming-first-token once warm.
- Sustained token/sec during burst: ~40k–60k tokens/sec aggregated across pool; per-connection throttles apply.
- Fallback: if burst pool exhausted, route to sync endpoint with queued acceptance and pushback headers.

Option B — Graceful degradation to lower-capacity model:
- Keep traffic on standard pool but fallback to a smaller quantized model when token/sec breaches threshold.
- TTFT: 100–200 ms best-case; quality delta documented.

Option C — Strict queuing/backpressure:
- Maintain streaming interface but return explicit 503 with Retry-After when the token/sec limit is hit; clients would need retry/backoff.

Operational notes:
- We can instrument telemetry to emit a "burst_mode" flag and expose first-token percentiles for the window; helpful for audit.
- We need your signoff on whether the 02:00–02:30 PT window is fixed and whether partial acceptance (drop ~5% of incoming jobs at peak) is tolerable.

I'll put a short tech appendix into the doc for Marissa.

—Karthik
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Alex Martin <alex.martin@brightbridge.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA carveout for nightly ingestion burst

Alex — thanks for laying out the need, and Karthik — great options. From a contracting perspective we recommend a time-limited addendum that includes:

- Window definition: 02:00–02:30 PT daily, on 2026-11-01 → 2026-12-31 (trial period).
- Performance tiers per option (e.g., "Burst pool: TTFT P50 <= 300ms; aggregate token/sec >= 40k").
- Explicit fallback behavior and customer notification requirements (if we switch to sync endpoint, BrightBridge must accept queued latency up to X minutes).
- Telemetry & verification: Redwood will publish hourly first-token percentiles and aggregate throughput for the window and allow BrightBridge to request a one-time audit export for the trial.
- Credits: if we miss the defined P50 TTFT by >30% for more than 3 days in the trial, apply a service credit equal to 5% of that month's usage for the trial.

Legal (Stephanie) — please prep a short addendum draft and we can run a quick redline pass. Alex — can you confirm the exact trial dates and whether procurement wants the addendum executed before Nov 1 or can accept retroactive coverage?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood-sla-draft-20261024.pdf (pdf)]

From: Alex Martin <alex.martin@brightbridge.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightbridge.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 25 Oct 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA carveout for nightly ingestion burst

Thanks all — this looks like a sensible path. Procurement prefers the addendum signed before Nov 1 if possible; otherwise we'll accept retroactive coverage but prefer an executed document for our auditors.

We accept Option A as the preferred fallback (burst pool + prefix caching). A few final asks:
- Please include the exact per-day expected throughput ceiling and the per-connection token/sec throttle in the addendum.
- Add an endpoint for the telemetry export (S3 location or secure link) and a schedule for the hourly reports.

If you can send the initial addendum draft and the operational playbook snippets this week, we'll route to procurement and legal on our side.

Alex
Director, Platform Engineering
BrightBridge Health

[Attachment: playbook-fallback-snippets.txt (text)]
